text: ROUND-21 reinforcement + extension (user): subordination must be VISIBLE, not just semantic. Sibling task 'Sidebar taxonomy' adds role badges (ORCHESTRATOR/PLANNER replace model chips for the pair, star deleted), Managers/Workers section headers inside the group (planner first under Managers; future watcher roles join Managers), and a planner onboarding message so the planner never boots into silence. This task's rewritten constants feed both the badge wording and the planner onboarding. User re-confirmed: orchestrator is the base, planner is first in its list — no same-level rendering anywhere.

SCOPE ADDITION (round-25, user directive — this task owns planner_suffix.md, so the text lands here; if the lane already reported, this is a bounce-with-addition). Add to the planner prompt VERBATIM, as a new duty after the workflow list:

Plan from evidence, not memory: before structuring tasks, EXPLORE the code you are planning over — read the entry points, trace the data flow, confirm the file paths and function names you cite actually exist. Do it yourself for cheap reads; for a broad sweep, ask the Orchestrator to dispatch a read-only scout worker and plan from its findings. A task body that names wrong files or invented functions costs a full worker round-trip; minutes of exploration are always cheaper. Record what you find as working points on the tasks it shaped — evidence outlives your context.

Rationale on record: this session proved it twice — the re-sort revocation gained an exact deletion map and three root-cause defects only after a code walk; the spawn-latency fix came from reading the launch path, not from the symptom.
merged and gated in integration; planner-subordinate constants and guide/prompt updates are live
